verification.method: scripts/verify/china.py reads the original UN files directly (not the site's generated data) and compares them with the built page, JSON-LD and CSV; the build itself fails if any sentence-level claim (assertClaim) stops being true; then a hand read of title, description, headline, FAQ and story text.
what: Population 1950–2100 (all table years), rank, share, decline rate and size, people lost per day, density, land area
Peak year (2021) and size, people lost since the peak
Births and deaths 2026, births 2016, fertility 2026 and record low (2023), highest fertility (1963)
Life expectancy 1958 and 1960; 1960 as the only year of decline 1950–2020 (build check)
Median age 1980, 2000, 2026, 2050, 2100 and first year above 50 (2044)
Urban share 1950, 2026, 2050, majority year (2011) and urban people; year below 1 billion (2070); 2100 total
Title, meta description, Article headline, FAQ answers in JSON-LD, CSV rows, falling live counter
against: UN WPP 2024 original file WPP2024_Demographic_Indicators_Medium.csv.gz (SHA-256 286ac36b…, downloaded 2026-11-25) and interim update zip (eb7846bf…) — 85 of 85 checks match
UN WUP 2025 original file WUP2025-F15-National-Definitions_percPop_by_category.xlsx (SHA-256 5fdc43a9…, downloaded 2026-11-25); licence CC BY 3.0 IGO stated in the file
Smil V., "China's great famine: 40 years later", BMJ 1999 (PubMed Central PMC1127087): famine spring 1959 to end of 1961, origin in the Great Leap Forward
